text:
mara: Heads-up — I started onboarding hf/cerulean-13b into the catalog and ran an int4 conversion smoke + eval. Seeing a weird drop in summarization ROUGE vs our fp16 baseline (~6 points). Not huge but reproducible across our prompt set. anyone seen similar with a proj-order or token-id mapping issue?

oliver: can you paste the eval numbers and config you used?

mara: quick paste: 
```
baseline fp16 (ref): rougeL=42.3, ppl=11.6
int4 quant (default converter): rougeL=36.1, ppl=12.9
int4 with per-channel scale tweak: rougeL=37.0, ppl=12.6
```
Conversion: hf -> internal format via convert_cerulean.py with --proj-order=auto (we forced a transpose in loader because shapes mismatched). Tokenizer: hf tokenizer v2 (unchanged).

jon: transpose forcing rings alarm bells. could be that projection order (in_proj/out_proj even/odd) got swapped — downstream rotary/rope indexing will diverge. do you have a short decode log (first 30 tokens logits) to diff against fp16?

mara: i ran a deterministic seed decode on the same prompt and dumped first 20 logits. fp16 vs int4 differ starting at token 5, logits delta > 0.5 for top tokens. snippet: 
```
prompt: "Summarize: Redwood Inference is..."
fp16 top logits token ids: [42, 773, 11, 5, 90, ...]
int4 top logits token ids: [42, 773, 99, 5, 90, ...]
```
That's a token swap at position 3.

sree: @mara can you also check the embedding vector for BOS/<s> token between fp16 and int4 (before any rotary applied)? if the embedding projection was transposed we should see a systematic permute or sign flip. also check kv-cache token id alignment (kvcache assumes same token ids) — vocab mapping issues are common with cerulean exports.

mara: ran embedding compare (cosine): bos embedding cos=0.86 between fp16 and int4. not identical. sample dims: fp16[:8]=[0.12, -0.03, 0.44, ...], int4[:8]=[0.11, 0.03, 0.43, ...] - note sign flip at idx 2.

jon: sign flip + earlier transpose hint => likely proj-order mismatch (we've seen a converter that reverses head inner ordering leading to even/odd head swap). that would change rotary phase pairing and cause early-token divergence. try running convert with --proj-order=headwise and run small eval.

mara: tried that, re-converted with --proj-order=headwise and re-ran the deterministic decode. logits now match through token 12 and rouge recovered to 40.1 (still ~2 behind fp16). ppl improved to 11.9. progress. :thumbsup:

oliver: nice. can you also try disabling rotary normalization/scale in runtime (flag --rotary-scale=0) to see if residual gap is rotary-scaling-related vs quant rounding? and run a small LM-eval compare (summary retention) for 50 examples.

mara: did a quick run with --rotary-scale=0, rouge=39.8 (tiny drop vs headwise convert). so quant rounding still accounts for ~1.5 rouge. suspect int4 attention kernel rounding for large heads.

sree: for the remaining delta, try per-channel quant (pcq) for the heavy proj matrices and leave small ones symmetric. also run a short ablation: int8 on attention only, int4 elsewhere. should show whether attention quant error is the culprit.

mara: scheduling those runs now. filing a short ticket: MODEL-ONB-477 cerulean-13b int4 regression — notes about proj-order, forced transpose, bos-cos 0.86, partial recovery with --proj-order=headwise, follow-up pcq/int8-attn ablations. adding logs and the deterministic decode artifacts to the ticket.

deploy-bot: Deployment job 7812 created for model cerulean-13b (staging) by mara.

mara: thanks all — will post results in this thread once ablations finish. if anyone wants to pair on the converter details, ping me. :coffee:
